guitar.evidence: Sonny Boy Williamson (either I or II) was primarily a harmonica player/vocalist, not a guitarist; backing guitarists varied across sessions.
guitar.notes: Correctly left unknown — not a guitar-led act.

tone.target: gritty 60s blues harp-guitar with slight fuzz edge
tone.profile: gritty 60s blues harp-guitar with slight fuzz edge
tone.summary: A gritty 60s blues harp tone achieved with a Fuzz distortion, followed by an AC30-style amp simulation, adding subtle tremolo for character.

rig.name: Sonny Boy Williamson - Help Me - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and background noise.
Provide the required gritty fuzz texture and mid-forward grit.
Optional secondary boost for added grit (kept inactive to prioritize fuzz).
blocks.gap: The primary drive is Fuzz; Green OD would be too polished.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the dry, small tube combo sound characteristic of 60s blues.
Provide a classic British cabinet sound that complements the AC30 tone.
blocks.gap: A smaller 2x12 might be ideal for 'small-amp feel', but UK Vintage 4x12 is the best available option.

blocks.purpose: Introduce the subtle vibrato effect requested (using Chorus as a substitute for dedicated Vibrato/Tremolo).
blocks.gap: No dedicated Vibrato module is available; Chorus provides a usable, subtle modulation.

blocks.purpose: Implement the required subtle vibrato/tremolo effect.
Add a touch of natural space without sounding modern or big.
blocks.gap: The 'dry and raw' mandate suggests minimal reverb, but Room is the least intrusive choice.

improvements.summary: Replace the large 4x12 cabinet with a smaller, more compact IR to achieve the desired small-amp feel.

proposals.recommendedAsset: small combo/2x12 IR (e.g., Fender Deluxe or Vox AC2)
proposals.reason: The 4x12 is too large; a smaller cab will better simulate the 'dry small-amp feel' of blues harp.
